successors.name: Parthian Empire
successors.text: 'the western part of the empire, including Mesopotamia' (Osroes I page, Vologases III page): Seleucia and Ctesiphon, 'the capitals of the Parthians'; Babylonia without Characene's Al-Basrah and…

ledger.x: 110: Osroes I, who revolted against Pacorus II in 109, rules the west of the Parthian Empire against Vologases III in the east.
116: Trajan takes Seleucia and Ctesiphon and puts Osroes' son on the throne.
117: after Trajan's death the Roman hold ends and Osroes I is back.
129: Vologases III removes Osroes I and the Parthian Empire is one again.

wars.name: Parthian civil war of Osroes I and Vologases III
wars.outcome: The empire was divided for nineteen years, Osroes I holding the west and Mesopotamia, Vologases III the east; Vologases III removed Osroes in 129.

wars.name: Trajan's Parthian campaign (Osroes I)
wars.outcome: Trajan made Armenia a province (114), took Seleucia and Ctesiphon (116), reached the Persian Gulf and forced Characene to pay tribute, and set up Parthamaspates; after his death in 117 the Parthians reinstated Osroes.

certainty.note: A divided empire with no frontier described; the western half is a minimum reading.
